topics.definition: A transaction is a sequence of database operations treated as a single logical unit of work.
tips: A transaction either completes fully or not at all.

topics.definition: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability.
A transaction passes through Active, Partially Committed, Committed, Failed, Aborted and Terminated states.
Concurrency control ensures multiple transactions execute safely without conflicts.
topics.example: Two users update the same record.

topics.definition: Locks control access to database items during transactions.
topics.example: Lock a row before updating it.

topics.definition: A deadlock occurs when two or more transactions wait indefinitely for each other.
topics.syntax: T1 waits for T2; T2 waits for T1

topics.definition: Recovery restores the database after failures using logs, checkpoints and backups.
COMMIT permanently saves changes, while ROLLBACK undoes uncommitted changes.
tips: Use COMMIT only after verifying changes.
